title: Evaluator fixture 0.1
description: Evaluator-private response and outcome assertions for one case, derived deterministically from the upstream possible-answer field and stored apart from all runner-visible scenario data. It states what was expected, never how a verdict is reached: there is no pass rule, weighting, or threshold here, because those belong to the versioned evaluator rather than to the fixture. Never sent to a runner, an adapter, or a work-claim payload.

user_turn_count.description: How many of the reference turns correspond to a user turn in the normalized scenario. Upstream Base carries at least one record whose reference answer ends with a verification turn the user never asked for, so the two counts are not always equal. Recording the boundary keeps that trailing turn available to the evaluator instead of silently truncating it, and stops a later reader from assuming response_assertions[i] always pairs with turns[i].

response_assertions.description: One entry per user turn, in turn order, holding the calls the upstream reference answer makes on that turn after parsing. Parsing is structural only: the strings are turned into function names and argument values so the evaluator does not have to re-parse them, and no comparison semantics are implied.

outcome_assertions.description: The observable end-state facts the evaluator may request after the final turn. Fact names only: the contract never carries an expected value, and the evaluator alone decides whether an observed fact satisfies the reference answer.

expected_call.description: One parsed reference call. `arguments` is typed as leak_free_object so that even here, where the material is legitimately evaluator-private, a nested rubric or threshold cannot be smuggled in under an argument name and later copied outward with the rest of the record.

positional_arguments.description: Values the upstream string passed positionally. Kept ordered and separate from named arguments because binding them to parameter names would require a tool signature the importer deliberately does not have.
